story: Gary is at home under his golf cart seat, checking the battery tap and tucking the wiring out of sight in the hazy 85-degree afternoon. Donna has claimed pickleball court one at the Rec Center and is drilling third-shot drops while she waits for him. Hal sits content on his porch, watching the quiet loop and keeping an eye on the clock so he can carry his cornbread to Rosa's early. Rosa, hopeful about the afternoon, is headed down Magnolia Loop.
events: Gary (gary golf cart): Check the battery tap and pre-route wiring under the seat, nothing mounted outside
Donna (pickleball court 1): Take court one and practice third-shot drops until Gary arrives
Hal waited: Sitting on the porch watching the quiet loop, keeping track of the time so I leave for Rosa's with the cornbread and table well ahead of schedule.
Rosa headed to Magnolia Loop (the street).

gary.thought_process: Application's filed, wiring's labeled and bench-tested, hardware's staged by the cart. Nothing more I can legally do to the exterior until the review board signs off (L-01). Parade is Halloween, a week out, so no panic. Nobody's around to talk to. Best use of this hour is tinkering on the cart's interior-side prep that isn't visible from the street, like pre-routing wiring and checking the battery tap, so mounting is quick once approval lands. Nothing mounted, nothing visible, nothing to answer for.

parameters.content: Check the battery tap and pre-route wiring under the seat, nothing mounted outside

donna.thought_process: I'm at the Rec Center and nobody's around. I checked the ladder board last tick and reserved a 2-hour slot at the kiosk for Gary and me to work on third-shot drops. Reservation's done, so there's no point fussing with the kiosk again. Gary isn't in sight, so I can't talk to him. Best use of this hour is to take a court and start drilling third-shot drops on my own so we're ahead when he shows up. L-05 caps me at 2 hours, which I've got covered.

parameters.content: Take court one and practice third-shot drops until Gary arrives

hal.thought_process: It's 2:17 PM and Saturday dinner at Rosa's is tonight. The cornbread and table plan is already written down and I've checked it twice. Nobody's on the street, and the flamingos are behind the hedge, so there's nothing to report. Gary filed his paperwork, and I'd rather keep things friendly with Donna than rush to the committee. Best use of this hour is to stay put on the porch, keep an eye on the loop, and leave on time with the cornbread and table. No fuss, no being late like last time.

parameters.content: Sitting on the porch watching the quiet loop, keeping track of the time so I leave for Rosa's with the cornbread and table well ahead of schedule.

rosa.thought_process: It's 2:17 PM and the table is set with Hal, Gary and Donna seated side by side. The main dish is done and holding warm, and my shift schedule is clear. The Halloween flyer on the Loop board is worth a look, since it might affect my neighbors' plans, and a short walk would calm my nerves. But I shouldn't wander far with guests coming tonight. A quick trip to Magnolia Loop to check the board and see whether anyone's around to remind about the dinner is a good use of this hour.

parameters.content: Everything's ready here, so I'll take a short walk to the Loop, check the Halloween flyer, and remind a neighbor or two about tonight's dinner.

laws.title: Cart Modifications
laws.text: Exterior golf cart modifications visible from the street require Architectural Review approval.

laws.title: Lawn Ornaments
laws.text: No more than 3 decorative ornaments may be visible from the street.

laws.title: Quiet Hours
laws.text: No amplified sound from 10 PM to 7 AM.

laws.title: Holiday Decor
laws.text: Holiday lighting is permitted from Thanksgiving through January 15.

laws.title: Court Reservations
laws.text: Pickleball courts may be reserved for a maximum of 2 hours per party.

laws.title: Parking
laws.text: No parking on the grass. Carts and cars stay on driveways or the street.
